findings.title: Collective raised status
findings.claim: The passive plural presents the whole quoted group as people who are to be raised.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mabuthun is a passive participle in the masculine plural; that ending meets the first-person plural in inna and assigns the resulting raised status to the entire speaking group.
findings.reader_payoff: The question concerns the group together, held in one resulting state.
findings.containment: This describes the local participial form; the agent remains unnamed and the questioned raising remains a question.

epistemic.reason: The accepted focus alignment and trusted morphology directly support the plural passive reading.

findings.title: The unnamed raiser
findings.claim: The passive predicate foregrounds the speakers as those acted upon while leaving the raiser grammatically unspoken.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mabuthun marks a passive patient; the quoted first-person plural supplies the affected group, so attention settles on their status rather than an agent.
findings.reader_payoff: The challenge is voiced from the side of the people who would undergo the act.
findings.containment: The form suppresses an agent in this clause; it does not identify or deny who that agent is.

epistemic.reason: The passive morphology is explicit in the accepted QAC alignment and in the trusted candidate support.

findings.title: Raising specified as new creation
findings.claim: The final creation phrase specifies the raised state as a new creation.
findings.mechanism: The passive carrier mabuthun meets the following accusative khalqan jadidan; the phrase attaches to the raised predicate and changes the question from bare raising to raising in a newly created state.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears what kind of raising the speakers challenge.
findings.containment: The creation phrase qualifies the questioned predicate and leaves its asserted truth unresolved.

epistemic.reason: Local attachment and the supplied focus morphology support the predicate-plus-qualifier relation.

findings.title: The predicate under emphasis
findings.claim: Mabuthun supplies the raised-status predicate governed by the emphatic particle inna.
findings.mechanism: The carrier participle follows inna and is the clause predicate; the following creation phrase then further qualifies that status, giving the question a predicate before its final specification.
findings.reader_payoff: The clause first establishes the proposed status and then sharpens it.
findings.containment: This is a syntactic account of the quoted question, not an assertion that the event occurs.

epistemic.reason: The local particle and predicate relation are supplied in the focus morphology and trusted analysis.

findings.title: Weight at the predicate
findings.claim: The emphatic onset and long plural ending give the resurrection predicate audible weight.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mabuthun is preceded by the bound emphatic lam and closes with plural length; their contact makes emphasis arrive with the predicate itself.
findings.reader_payoff: The question's central verb is heard as a marked landing rather than an unweighted continuation.
findings.containment: This is a bounded sound observation accompanying the ordinary passive plural meaning.

epistemic.reason: The focus form supports the sound pattern; its perceptual weight is an interpretive effect rather than a separate lexical sense.

findings.title: Motion from stillness
findings.claim: The local resurrection predicate can retain the root's pressure of stirring what lies still, while its passive form and complement specify the questioned event as resurrection.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mabuthun meets the bones-and-fragments condition and the following new-creation phrase; that contact lets the root's stillness-to-motion branch color the local raising without turning it into a mission or journey.
findings.reader_payoff: The question presses the transition from bodily stillness toward renewed action.
findings.containment: The local passive resurrection reading remains intact; the directional sending branch is excluded because no task or destination is supplied.

epistemic.reason: The trusted word analysis supports the root-range relation, while the local syntax bounds it to the resurrection predicate.

findings.claim: The adjective jadidan qualifies khalqan, placing newness on the creation phrase rather than on the raising predicate alone.

findings.title: Creation under skeptical pressure

findings.mechanism: The carrier khalqan names creation; the paired interrogative and emphatic particles supply the independent skeptical trigger, so the word for forming something can echo the possibility of a fabricated claim without replacing its local sense.

epistemic.reason: The trusted root-range support and local interrogative surface ground the relation, while the fabrication reading remains a bounded contextual resonance.
